messages:
maria: Quick sync - need to finalize battlecard + follow-up flow for the Redwood webinar. Focus: competitive plays vs cloud-managed endpoints and infra vendors. I uploaded the current deck and the SDR play draft: https://docs.google.com/yyy.

alex: Scanned the deck. Two guardrails: 1) avoid head-to-head vendor naming in public slides; 2) make the follow-up email actionable with a CTA that maps to routing tags (so we can measure conversions by claim).

jonah: Bench summary for combiner slide: internal runs show notable reductions in 95p latency under burst scenarios when routing favors local KV caches and continuous batching. Recommend we say: "Significant 95p latency reductions in our internal benchmarks; contact us for test details." Legal will want the caveat.

kevin: Sales ask: add two quick rebuttals for "Why not just use cloud provider endpoints?"
- Rebuttal A: "Managed endpoints hide unit-economics and make burst costs unpredictable. Redwood gives routing and caching to control cost at scale."
- Rebuttal B: "Vendor endpoints can vary in latency across regions and model sizes; Redwood offers predictable SLOs and rollout controls."

sara: For the landing hero, my preferred headline: "Run LLM inference with production-grade latency and cost controls." Subhead: "Batching, caching, and routing that cut token cost and tame tail latency 1x better visibility." (we'll probably A/B test cost vs latency stat).

maria: Reword the subhead to avoid an unverified multiplier. Maybe: "Batching, caching, and routing that reduce token cost and tame tail latency  contact us for methodology"

alex: On routing & tracking: proposal for the form handler tags:
```
if source == 'webinar' and interest == 'infra':
  team = 'solutions-infra'
  tags += ['webinar','interest:infra','lead:cold']
elif source == 'webinar' and interest == 'prod':
  team = 'sdr-webinar'
  tags += ['webinar','interest:production','lead:warm']
```
This keeps routing easy and lets us filter by interest in SFDC.

jonah: Legal note: please don't publish the numeric percent without a link to methodology. I'll hand a 1-paragraph methodology blurb to alex by EOD. It will reference internal replay traces, model families, and hardware baseline.

kevin: For the battlecard one-pager, can we add an "Objection -> Counter" table for the top 3 managed-endpoint claims? Drafts: 
- Objection: "Lower ops overhead on vendor endpoints" -> Counter: "Redwood reduces ops via unified runtime + autoscaling, and adds observability and rollout controls other vendors don't expose."
- Objection: "Vendor SLAs are enough" -> Counter: "SLAs are about availability; our value is predictable latency and token economics under production workloads."

sara: Opsbot reminder: assets due Tue EOD: landing copy, SDR one-pager, and benchmark appendix.

maria: Action items:
- Alex: open legal review for any % claim (due Tue AM)
- Jonah: methodology blurb for field by EOD today
- Kevin: draft the 3 objection counters in the battlecard by Tue noon
- Alex + EngInfra: implement tags in staging by Wed so routing is live before email send

alex: I'll create the tagging PR and ping eng-infra. Also will add a measurement tag for claim variant (A/B) so we can tie clicks back to which hero they saw.

maria: Great. Let's aim to lock the hero by Monday so design can finalize slides. We'll avoid naming competitors in slides and instead use "managed endpoints" or "vendor endpoints" in the public narrative. Thanks team. :ribbon:
